worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}{y}^{3}-{y}^{2}+x) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}{y}^{3}-{y}^{2}+x) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}-{y}^{4}-2) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}-{y}^{4}-2)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x{y}^{3}+1 & 3{x}^{2}{y}^{2}-2y \\ 3{x}^{2} & -4{y}^{3}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}2x{y}^{3}+1 & 3{x}^{2}{y}^{2}-2y \\ 3{x}^{2} & -4{y}^{3}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}{y}^{3}-{y}^{2}+x \\ {x}^{3}-{y}^{4}-2\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-{[\begin{aligned}2x{y}^{3}+1 & 3{x}^{2}{y}^{2}-2y \\ 3{x}^{2} & -4{y}^{3}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}{y}^{3}-{y}^{2}+x \\ {x}^{3}-{y}^{4}-2\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}2(2)(-1)^{3}+1 & 3(2)^{2}(-1)^{2}-2(-1) \\ 3(2)^{2} & -4(-1)^{3}\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}(2)^{2}(-1)^{3}-(-1)^{2}+2 \\ (2)^{3}-(-1)^{4}-2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}-3 & 14 \\ 12 & 4\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{(-3)\cdot 4-14\cdot 12}[\begin{aligned}4 & -14 \\ -12 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{180}[\begin{aligned}-82 \\ 21\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{139}{90} \\ -\frac{53}{60}\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}1.544 \\ -0.883\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
html:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function f:Rn→Rn is

xn+1=xn−[Jf(xn)]−1f(xn),

where Jf(xn) is the Jacobian of f evaluated at xn.

In our case, the Jacobian is

Jf(x)=[∂∂x(x2y3−y2+x)∂∂y(x2y3−y2+x)∂∂x(x3−y4−2)∂∂y(x3−y4−2)]=[2xy3+13x2y2−2y3x2−4y3].

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

xn+1=xn−[2xy3+13x2y2−2y3x2−4y3]xn−1[x2y3−y2+xx3−y4−2]xn.

Starting with x0=[2−1], we have

x1=x0−[2xy3+13x2y2−2y3x2−4y3]x0−1[x2y3−y2+xx3−y4−2]x0=[2−1]−[2(2)(−1)3+13(2)2(−1)2−2(−1)3(2)2−4(−1)3]−1[(2)2(−1)3−(−1)2+2(2)3−(−1)4−2]=[2−1]−[−314124]−1[−35]=[2−1]−1(−3)⋅4−14⋅12[4−14−12−3][−35]=[2−1]+1180[−8221]=[13990−5360]≈[1.544−0.883],

rounded to three decimal places.
